description: ctx config write creates the VS Code or Cursor MCP file from editor_mcp_config.
acceptanceCriteria: editor_mcp_config('vscode', command, home) returns config_type stdio, that command, mcp_arg mcp, and ctx_home home. editor_mcp_config('cursor', command, home) returns config_type as an empty string and the same command, mcp_arg, and ctx_home.
constraints: Do not invent a second tool name.
Cursor output uses an empty config_type so the written file omits type.
Write .vscode/mcp.json or .cursor/mcp.json. Merge an existing JSON file. Leave an invalid file untouched.
workerGuidance: Small local model rule: solve only the active subtask. Do not implement later CTX tasks early.
Every test function for this task's subtasks must contain that slice token, for example CTX_087_1.
After writing or changing a test, always call the declared pytest command before ending the turn. Do not stop with explanation text only.
If the active subtask's verification already passes because earlier work implemented it correctly, run the declared command and mark the subtask done. Do not rewrite unrelated files.
Keep edits inside targetArtifacts unless the subtask explicitly says otherwise.
When writing tests, assert only the current subtask's scope so later subtasks still have meaningful work.

instructions: Name the test function so it contains CTX_087_1.

editor_mcp_config(client, command, home) for client vscode returns config_type stdio, command, mcp_arg mcp, and ctx_home home.
ctx config write --client vscode --workspace PATH writes .vscode/mcp.json from this dict. The args are -m, context_mgmt, mcp. env CTX_HOME is the home.
